title: Students and teachers call for mobilisation and strikes over university funding in Paris
seoTitle: Paris student and teacher strike called

tea.why: Protesters say government responses to months of mobilization are insufficient and a decade of austerity has weakened universities.
tea.want: 150,000 new higher education places, staff recruitment, higher budgets, better pay, and the abolition of Parcoursup and Mon Master.
tea.changed: Nov 23: A coalition of higher education unions and student organizations called for nationwide strikes and rallies on November 26.

summary: Following two months of protests, an inter-union coalition representing higher education staff and students has called for a nationwide day of strikes, rallies, and demonstrations on November 26. Organizers state that government measures, including the announcement of 20,000 additional higher education places, fall short after years of austerity. The coalition demands the creation of 150,000 university places, a multi-year recruitment and tenure plan, higher funding for public research and universities, and the repeal of the Parcoursup and Mon Master admissions systems. Additionally, participants are calling for increased student grants and higher salaries for public agents. The government previously announced plans to reform and eventually replace Parcoursup by 2028, along with indexing student grants to inflation.
demands: Implement a multi-year recruitment and tenure plan
Increase funding for universities and public laboratories
Revalue student grants and staff salaries
response: The government announced the creation of 20,000 additional higher education places, the evolution of Parcoursup starting in 2027 before its replacement in 2028, and the indexation of student grants to inflation, though unions dismissed these measures as insufficient.

updates.text: Unions and student groups issued a joint call for nationwide strikes and demonstrations on November 26.
